findings.location: library/functional-analysis/continuous-functional-calculus-for-self-adjoint-and-normal-operators-examples.md, closing paragraph, sentence "And the same nilpotent, whose quadratic form takes the non-real value i/2 at a unit vector, shows that nonnegativity of the spectrum does not characterise positivity once self-adjointness is dropped."
findings.evidence: Item ex-square-root-and-absolute-value-of-a-matrix defines T = [[0,2],[0,0]] (twice the unit Jordan block J = [[0,1],[0,0]]) and computes |T| = diag(0,2); item cex-self-adjointness-cannot-be-dropped-from-the-order-calculus uses J = [[0,1],[0,0]] and computes <Jx,x> = i/2 at x = (e_1 + i e_2)/sqrt(2). For the first item's operator the same unit vector gives <Tx,x> = 2*(i/2) = i, so the sentence's "the same nilpotent" with the value i/2 is false, and the earlier phrase "the nilpotent Jordan block" in the same paragraph also names 2J rather than the Jordan block. Both items are mathematically correct; this is a summary-prose misattribution in a B page, which the reader is not licensed to edit.
